title.narrative: NIHR-HSPR-PA-Developing a National Integrated Digital platform for AMR Data Surveillance and Management in Uganda

description.narrative:
The project will develop, implement and evaluate the National Integrated Anti-Microbial Resistance (NIAMR) Digital Platform which will be designed to integrate and share data generated in health facilities across Uganda to support rapid detection and monitoring of AMR, and inform scaling of the platform across other One Health sectors (i.e. animal health, environment, water and wildlife). This initiative bridges the gap between raw laboratory data and actionable public health intelligence. By creating a unified national picture of resistance patterns and quickly identifying resistance hotspots, the platform aims to support better patient care, guide treatment policies and target interventions more effectively. Beyond the technology, the project implements comprehensive training and protocols to empower a wide range of stakeholders (frontline health workers, communities, researchers and policy makers) to use digital data to improve health outcomes and national antimicrobial stewardship. This work involves assessing current data systems, co-designing the platform with stakeholders, piloting it in selected regions, and evaluating its impact on surveillance and clinical decision-making. The goal is to establish a sustainable, scalable tool that enables data-driven action to reduce the burden of AMR in Uganda with future potential to include animal, water and environmental health AMR data. The NIAMR Project is a collaborative project between Makerere University, the Ministry of Health, Mbarara University of Science and Technology and the Baylor College of Medicine, Uganda. The project will be undertaken in Uganda from February 2026 to January 2029 (3 years).
The project addresses the critical problem of AMR in Uganda where it is a leading public health security problem. The major challenge is that valuable AMR data generated in health facilities remains siloed and unavailable for decision-making.

This project has 5 objectives: 1. To analyse the current landscape, challenges and opportunities of anti-microbial resistance (AMR) data management in Uganda. 2. To co-develop and implement a National Integrated AMR Digital Platform for capturing, processing and sharing of AMR data. 3. To evaluate the platform’s impact on improving AMR surveillance, clinical decision-making and identification of resistance hotspots. 4. To assess the platform’s feasibility, acceptability, and usability among healthcare workers, policy makers and other stakeholders. 5. To plan for the platform’s sustainable scale-up nationally and its future expansion to other One Health sectors.
